presentation.label: LIVE REC RETRIG FIX
presentation.summary: LIVE RECORDING records every pad retrig hit as a real trig, with the velocity and timing you played.
presentation.overview: Stock records a retrig hold as one trig and a few locks that its held-note erase mostly removes, so what plays back is not what you played. With Live Rec Retrig Fix every hit of a roll, from RTRG + pad or a pad set to ALWAYS ON, records a real trig at the velocity it sounded and the time it sounded, quantize live rec on or off. Rates faster than a step record a trig with a step retrig, because a step holds one trig. There is nothing to set.
highlights: One real trig for each hit at 1/16 and slower, velocity following pressure.
ALWAYS ON pads record the same way.
Quantize live rec applies to retrig hits as to any note.
Faster rates record a step retrig, and the RETRIG menu's VEL.CUR goes with it.
Pad retrigs fall on the sequencer's swung grid while it plays, and a recorded roll starts on that grid.
usage: Hold RECORD and press PLAY, hold RTRG and hold a pad, varying the pressure.
Let go and leave LIVE RECORDING: the roll plays back as played.
In GRID RECORDING, edit the roll's trigs one by one.

access.location: LIVE RECORDING, with RTRG + pad or a pad set to ALWAYS ON. The QUANT RTRG TO SEQ checkbox is the last row of GLOBAL > CONTROL > SEQUENCER CONFIG.
steps: Hold RTRG, then hold a pad and vary the pressure.

controls.name: QUANT RTRG TO SEQ
controls.doc: Checkbox in GLOBAL > CONTROL > SEQUENCER CONFIG, after SAMPLE POS RES. Checked puts pad retrigs on the swung grid while the sequencer plays and records a roll's first trig on it. YES turns it over, RIGHT checks, LEFT unchecks. Kept with the project.

limitations: Rates faster than a step record one velocity for each trig's hits, or VEL.CUR's fade.
Micro timing has 24 units a step.
A roll started before LIVE RECORDING can miss hits.
This merged build has run on one unit, on the builds TESTING.md names.
The press sounds where it was played; only its recorded trig moves to the grid, and not when the grid point is more than a step away.
